{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement

**To:** Deal team (Sparkling)  
**From:** Legal  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Garman Software License and Maintenance Agreement  
**Status:** All findings below are verified (verification: pass).

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. Of nineteen rules assessed, **thirteen are compliant**, **six require action** — five deviations and two gaps where no usable clause exists (transition assistance and vendor insurance; six action items in total).

The commercial architecture is unusually favourable to us in several respects: the licence is perpetual while fees are paid (§ 17(a)), we may terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no exit fee (§ 17(b)), there is no auto-renewal, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no exclusivity or non-compete, no audit right against us, no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, and no "AS IS" disclaimer to swallow the express conformance warranty in § 12. The IP indemnity in § 13 sits at the fallback and is carved out of the liability cap and consequential-damages exclusion in § 15, which is better than the fallback super-cap.

The exposure is concentrated in five areas. First, **§ 15 contains no monetary cap at all**, leaving our direct-damages exposure unlimited. Second, **§ 13 vests ownership of the bespoke Modifications we commission and pay for in Garman**, and the Agreement is silent on ownership of our own data even though Garman converts and handles it under § 4(b). Third, **assignment is blanket-prohibited for us** (§§ 3(c) and 20(d)) with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, and the licence is expressly non-transferable and does not extend to contractors acting on our behalf. Fourth, **§ 19 is a mutual no-hire, not a non-solicit**, reaching any employee of the other party with no advertising carve-out. Fifth, there is **no transition-assistance or data-return obligation on Garman** and **no insurance requirement anywhere**, notwithstanding that Garman installs on-premises and handles our data.

Three of these sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and are set out in Section 3 below. Governing law (Nova Scotia) is a deviation but a low-heat one: it is our home forum and the jurisdiction grant is non-exclusive.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note / proposed action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 13 (Intellectual Property Indemnity) | At the fallback, and above it on the cap: § 15 carves § 13 out of the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion. No reverse indemnity anywhere. Sub-elements to raise in negotiation only: no express defend/control-of-defence mechanic, no refund limb if (a)–(c) fail, IP/title matters only, affiliates unnamed, tight 10-calendar-day notice. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 | Garman owns all IP in the Work including the bespoke Schedule "D" Modifications; our only rights are the § 2 non-exclusive, non-transferable licence with no modify or sublicense right (§ 3). No statement that we retain rights in our data. **Redline:** add a Sparkling data-ownership sentence and a perpetual licence back over the bespoke Modifications. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 15 (Limitation of Garman's Liability) | § 15 is the only liability provision and contains **no monetary cap**; direct-damages exposure is unlimited for both parties. Fails preferred and fallback. **Redline:** mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000; retain existing §§ 13/14 carve-outs and add indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement as uncapped Excluded Claims; confirm our fee obligations are not "damages". |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | Page 10 (§ 20(d); § 3(c)) | Blanket consent requirement with no reasonableness standard and no affiliate/successor carve-out; § 3(c) bars our assignment altogether except as Garman authorises at its discretion. Walk-away territory. **Redline:** affiliate/successor carve-out, reasonableness standard on consent, no assignment by Garman to a competitor, conform § 3(c). |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 (Grant of License) | Perpetual and extends to our affiliates, but expressly non-transferable with no successor-transfer right (§§ 3(c), 20(d)), and contractors/outsourced providers acting on our behalf are not covered. **Redline:** contractor use at the Authorized Locations and transfer to a successor on merger or sale of the business, preserving Garman's consent right otherwise and the Authorized Locations limits. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 2 | No exclusivity or sole-source obligation on us; § 2 grant is non-exclusive, § 3 restrictions are licence-scope only, § 10 maintenance is a renewable one-year term with no sole-source support obligation. Meets preferred position. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 17 (Term and Termination) | No liquidated damages, penalty, late-payment interest or early-termination charge payable by us; § 17(b) exit carries no fee, and § 19 carries no placement fee. Meets preferred position. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 3 (Restrictions on Use) | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction; § 3 is confined to ordinary licence-scope protections. § 19 is a personnel covenant addressed under NOSOLICIT. Meets preferred position. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 17(b) | Unconditional customer right on 90 days' notice with no exit cost (top of the 60–90 day fallback range; no fee is better than the fallback). Garman has no convenience right. Noted only: no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the § 17(c) refund applies on Garman default). |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 | No licence-verification, inspection or audit right runs against us anywhere. Better than preferred; benefits our party, so no redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) | Nova Scotia law and non-exclusive Nova Scotia jurisdiction; Nova Scotia is not an accepted law, so both material terms fail. Not walk-away: our home province, non-exclusive grant, no arbitration clause. **Redline:** New York law and exclusive New York County venue; Delaware, California or England and Wales/London available as fallback. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 11 (Fees) | No MFN or most-favoured-customer obligation burdening us. Note: no MFN in our favour either — a commercial point if pricing benchmarking is wanted. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 11 | No minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap; fees per the Fee Schedule only, extra fees only if we use the Software beyond the Authorized Locations (§ 2). **Open item:** Schedule "A" is not reproduced — confirm it carries no committed user/location counts or minimum annual maintenance spend. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | **Deviation** | § 19 (Non-Solicitation of Employees) | Drafted as a **no-hire**, not a non-solicit, reaching "any employee of the other party" with the "directly involved" qualifier attaching only to the former-employee limb, and no advertising carve-out. Walk-away territory despite being mutual and 12 months. **Redline:** convert to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs; delete the no-hire. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 10 (Maintenance and Support) | No auto-renewal; renewable one-year maintenance term requiring affirmative agreement, perpetual licence while fees are paid, and 90-day exit. Meets preferred position. Noted only: no renewal uplift cap and no reminder mechanic — raise the CPI/3% cap in the Fee Schedule negotiation. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 17 | Exit obligations run one way (we cease use and certify destruction); no transition-assistance, data-export or deletion mechanic anywhere (§ 8(b) is limited to rejection, § 4 to implementation conversion, § 16 to escrow release). Fallback also unmet. **Redline:** new § 17(d) — up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, return of our data within 30 days in machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 12 (Specifications and Warranty) | Conformance warranty through acceptance, a full year from the Maintenance Commencement Date and for as long as Maintenance Services continue — at or above preferred. Real remedies (§ 10(c) no-charge repair; § 8(b) full refund on rejection) and **no AS IS or implied-warranty disclaimer anywhere**. Sub-elements noted: no separate services, compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranties; repair rather than an express repair/replace/refund election. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Page 10 (§ 20) | The word "insurance" does not appear; no coverage or certificate requirement in §§ 20(a)–(i), § 4 or § 9, despite Garman installing on-premises and converting our data (§ 4(a)–(b)). Walk-away territory. **Redline:** insert model coverage as new § 20(j); offer E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback in the comment. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

Three findings fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading chips:

1. **Assignment (§§ 3(c), 20(d))** — a blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out. We must have the affiliate/successor carve-out and a reasonableness standard on consent.
2. **No-hire (§ 19)** — a no-hire covering all Vendor personnel, untethered to the engagement. Must be narrowed to a non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with the standard carve-outs.
3. **Vendor insurance (§ 20)** — no insurance obligation at all for an on-premises vendor with access to our data. Must be inserted.

We would also treat the **absence of any liability cap in § 15** as non-negotiable in substance: unlimited direct-damages exposure fails both the preferred and fallback positions on a material term, and the fix is a single insertion into the existing sentence.

Items expressly **not** in walk-away territory, and therefore available to trade: IP ownership of the Modifications (nothing assigns our IP or data to Garman), licence transferability (the grant is perpetual and covers our affiliates), and governing law (our home forum, non-exclusive jurisdiction, no arbitration).

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six action items: § 13 (data ownership plus licence back over the bespoke Modifications), § 15 (mutual cap and Excluded Claims), §§ 3(c)/20(d) and § 2 (assignment carve-out, reasonableness standard, contractor use, successor transfer), § 19 (non-solicit conversion), new § 17(d) (transition assistance and data return) and new § 20(j) (insurance).
2. **Sequence the negotiation** around the walk-away items and the liability cap first; hold governing law back as a concession item, noting that Delaware, California or England and Wales/London are acceptable fallbacks.
3. **Obtain Schedule "A" (Fee Schedule) and Schedule "D" (Modifications)** and confirm Schedule "A" contains no committed user/location counts or minimum annual maintenance spend, and that Schedule "D" matches the Modifications we intend to own or licence back.
4. **Raise in the Fee Schedule negotiation rather than by redline:** a CPI/3% cap on renewal-period maintenance uplift, and (optionally) MFN-style pricing benchmarking, which the Agreement does not currently provide in either direction.
5. **Reserve for the second pass, as sub-elements only:** the § 13 indemnity mechanics (defend/control of defence, refund limb, affiliates, the 10-day notice period), an express pro-rata refund on convenience termination under § 17(b), and services/compliance-with-laws/no-malicious-code warranties in § 12.
6. **Confirm internally** that 90 days' notice under § 17(b) is operationally sufficient for exit planning, given that transition assistance is currently absent and would be introduced by our new § 17(d)."}
